problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,3\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-4)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{24}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{3\cdot 8}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{3})≈{19.47}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
